about: Findings of tools/game_audit.py that are known and accepted. Each entry needs a reason; matched findings are still counted and listed in the report under 'Allowed', never hidden. Fields: code (or '*'), area (substring of the area name or key), level (number or 'A-B,C'), key (regex on the decor or creature key), x, y, reason.

Pilgrim's Path: the dead twisted trees across the door of a cave or ruin are the game's burnable thicket (wilds.js wdThicket, wd_hills.js); burn them with a torch or lantern and the door is open, by design

The Oakwood: the dead twisted trees across the door of a hidden cave or ruin are the burnable thicket (wilds.js wdThicket); burned with a torch or lantern they are ash and the door is open, by design (the living oaks round each hill now have a way cut through them, wd_hills.js wdhTidy)

the hidden caves and ruins of the older outdoor maps (wilds.js, wd_hills.js): the dead twisted trees across each door are the burnable thicket, burned with a torch or lantern by design; the living trees round each hill now have a way cut through them (wd_hills.js wdhTidy)

Oldhaven, the Land Gate: the gate is two squares deep (rows 4 and 5); the party walks into its front square (row 5) and is carried to the Pilgrim's Path (walked in the game: 100,6 north goes to level 400). The back square only fills the gatehouse.
Oldhaven, the east gate: two squares deep (columns 144 and 145); the party walks into the front square at column 144. The back square only fills the gatehouse.
Oldhaven, the south gate to the quay: two squares deep (rows 144 and 145); the party walks into the front square at row 144. The back square only fills the gatehouse.
Oldhaven Quay, the great gate of the city: two squares deep (rows 8 and 9); the party walks into the front square at row 9. The back square only fills the gatehouse.
